name: Autoimmune Encephalitis

ethnicAssociations: Anti-LGI1 encephalitis has male predominance and affects older adults

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Graus et al. 2016 Clinical Approach to Diagnosis of Autoimmune Encephalitis

criteria.description: Subacute onset (rapid progression over <3 months) of working memory deficits, altered mental status, or psychiatric symptoms
At least one of: new focal CNS findings, seizures, CSF pleocytosis, MRI features suggestive of encephalitis
Specific neural antibody detected (NMDA-R, LGI1, CASPR2, AMPA-R, GABA-B-R, etc.)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Subacute onset of cognitive/psychiatric symptoms with at least one supportive feature (seizures, CSF pleocytosis, MRI changes, focal findings) and exclusion of alternative causes. Specific antibody detection provides definite diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Major subtypes: anti-NMDAR (most common, young women, ovarian teratoma), anti-LGI1 (older men, faciobrachial dystonic seizures, hyponatremia), anti-CASPR2 (Morvan syndrome, neuromyotonia), anti-GABA-B (seizures, limbic encephalitis). Seronegative AE exists.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Subacute cognitive decline with psychiatric features
pathognomonic.notes: Developing over days to weeks; confusion, memory impairment, personality change
Pathognomonic for anti-LGI1 encephalitis; brief unilateral arm and face jerking
Characteristic of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; lip smacking, jaw movements, choreoathetosis

common.notes: Psychosis, agitation, hallucinations, paranoia, catatonia; often initial presentation
Particularly short-term memory; characteristic of limbic involvement

occasional.notes: Tachycardia, blood pressure fluctuations, central hypoventilation in anti-NMDAR
Insomnia or hypersomnia; severe sleep disruption in anti-IgLON5
Reduced speech output progressing to mutism in anti-NMDAR

rare.notes: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis; may require mechanical ventilation
Morvan syndrome with anti-CASPR2: neuromyotonia, insomnia, autonomic dysfunction

laboratory: Serum and CSF neural antibody panels: NMDA-R, LGI1, CASPR2, AMPA-R, GABA-B-R, GABA-A-R, DPPX, IgLON5
CSF: lymphocytic pleocytosis (common in anti-NMDAR), elevated protein
CSF may be normal in anti-LGI1 encephalitis
Paraneoplastic antibody panel for intracellular antigens (Hu, CV2, Ma2, amphiphysin)
imaging: MRI FLAIR/T2: medial temporal lobe hyperintensity (limbic encephalitis pattern)
MRI may be normal in up to 50% of anti-NMDAR encephalitis
FDG-PET may show temporal lobe hypermetabolism or extratemporal abnormalities
CT/MRI/ultrasound for tumor screening (ovarian teratoma, thymoma, lung cancer)
genetic: No specific genetic cause for autoimmune encephalitis
HLA associations reported for some subtypes
other: EEG: diffuse or focal slowing, extreme delta brush pattern (anti-NMDAR), epileptiform discharges
Tumor screening: pelvic MRI/ultrasound (ovarian teratoma in anti-NMDAR), CT chest/abdomen (lung, thymus)
CSF antibody testing generally more sensitive than serum for cell-surface antibodies

distinguishingFeatures: CJD has cortical ribboning on DWI MRI
CJD progresses more rapidly with myoclonus and akinetic mutism
CJD does not respond to immunotherapy
MS has dissemination in space and time
MS has white matter lesions not limbic encephalitis pattern
HSE has acute onset with fever
HSE has hemorrhagic temporal lobe lesions
HSE has positive HSV PCR in CSF
Post-HSE autoimmune encephalitis can occur weeks later

redFlags: Young woman with new-onset psychosis should be evaluated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis before attributing to primary psychiatric disease
Autonomic instability and central hypoventilation in anti-NMDAR requires ICU management
Ovarian teratoma must be screened for in all female patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis
Post-herpes simplex encephalitis: anti-NMDAR encephalitis can develop weeks after viral infection
Faciobrachial dystonic seizures are often drug-resistant but respond to immunotherapy (anti-LGI1)
Intracellular antibodies (Hu, Ma2, CV2) indicate paraneoplastic etiology with aggressive tumor search needed
Early immunotherapy improves outcomes - do not delay treatment while waiting for antibody results
references: Graus F, et al. A clinical approach to diagnosis of autoimmune encephalitis. Lancet Neurol. 2016;15(4):391-404.
Dalmau J, et al. Autoimmune Encephalitis. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(9):840-851.
Titulaer MJ, et al. Treatment and prognostic factors for long-term outcome in patients with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis. Lancet Neurol. 2013;12(2):157-165.
